title: Wounds from the past
hook: trauma needs care; healing can take help and time
tomorrow: Pope Francis compared the Church to a hospital. what kind?

segments.voice: Yesterday, seventy times seven, and forgiveness that isn't excusing: begin somewhere. Today, what's left after you begin.

A car backfires, and someone across the parking lot ducks. A voice gets raised in another room, and a grown adult is suddenly a kid again. Some hurts live on long after the day itself. Old wounds last because they're wounds, not because the person is weak. And wounds need care.
screen: `A CAR BACKFIRES.` → `SUDDENLY A KID AGAIN.` → `WOUNDS NEED CARE.`

segments.voice: This week walked hard ground. One day at a time. Trusted again. Doubt was met. Near in the dark. He can take it. Begin somewhere. Today ties a knot on it. Remember Thomas: when the risen Jesus comes back, the wounds are still there. Rising didn't erase them; they became the way he was known. He showed them on purpose and invited Thomas to touch them. So Catholic teaching doesn't treat an old trauma as a failure of faith. It treats it as a wound, and wounds get care: a counselor, a doctor, a friend who doesn't rush you, the sacraments, time. A psalm pictures God doing slow work, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: he "healeth the broken of heart, and bindeth up their bruises." Binding is done again and again, a fresh dressing each day, and nobody tears off a bandage to check whether the cut is finished. The same patience belongs to the person carrying the wound. Forgiveness can begin, and the wound can still need tending. Healing takes time.
screen: `SIX LINES FROM A HARD WEEK.` · `THE RISEN JESUS KEPT HIS WOUNDS.` · `A WOUND GETS CARE.` · `HE BINDETH UP THEIR BRUISES.` · then, large: `HEALING TAKES TIME.`

segments.voice: Rest a hand on an old scar, or over your heart if there's no scar to find. Feel the skin that closed over something that once hurt. Breathe slowly, and let the sit be patient with whatever old wound comes to mind, without pressing on it.
Wounds from the past. Hurts that outlast the day they happened, and heal slowly, with care, help and time.
Keep this: healing takes time, and even the risen Jesus kept his scars. Until tomorrow, then.

howItsDone: Catholics bring old hurts to prayer and to the sacraments, and the Church encourages counseling and medical care for trauma alongside them; some parishes offer support groups or healing retreats.
